items.title: The secret of 'strange metals' may lie in quantum statistics, not collisions
items.summary: In an ordinary metal, electrons behave like well-defined particles that occasionally bump into imperfections or vibrations of the crystal. Many materials with strong electron–electron interactions, including the copper-oxide (cuprate) superconductors, break these rules. In these "strange metals," electrical resistance rises in a straight line with temperature over a very wide range. Electrons seem to lose their momentum at the fastest rate quantum mechanics allows, the so-called Planckian limit. What causes this is still an open question.

items.title: Pathogen P. aeruginosa uses protein to limit entry of last-resort antibiotic
items.summary: Bacteria have many strategies for defending themselves against antibiotics. Some destroy the drug, others pump it out or alter its target. They can also, more simply, prevent it from getting in. A team at the University of Geneva (UNIGE) has discovered how Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a bacterium responsible for infections that are often difficult to treat, very rapidly restricts the entry of imipenem, an antibiotic reserved for the most critical cases. Published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, these findings reveal a mechanism of antibiotic resistance and open up new avenues for eventually counteracting it.

items.title: Black gobies are growing larger despite climate change
items.summary: Researchers at the Department of Paleontology at the University of Vienna compared fossil and modern ear stones of the black goby (Gobius niger) from the northern Adriatic Sea to reconstruct its growth history over the past 8,000 years. The surprising result: while body size remained remarkably stable in the past, today's black gobies grow faster and reach larger sizes—even as the Adriatic Sea is warming rapidly. The study is now published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B.

Jamal Anderson was the last NFL running back to amass 500+ touches in a season, including the playoffs. That was in 1998. Jahmyr Gibbs could join him. NASCAR's new 2027 Clash format demands four tires and simulated fuel at 200 mph. Teams must master pit road speed limits or face time penalties. Under official supervision, a particular car configuration is required as teams traverse pit road. They cannot just drive a fast lap and go back to the garage. Final times start at the green flag and end at the checkered flag. A driver with the fastest car can still lose the pole if his crew misses a speed limit. Time penalties will be assessed for speeding or other pit stop infractions. It is a bold move that tests execution as much as raw speed.

The Steelers haven't won a road game against the Eagles in Philadelphia since 1965. Here's how the 11-game drought unfolded. The Pittsburgh Steelers have a long history with the Philadelphia Eagles, but their trips across the state line have been anything but successful in recent decades. Pittsburgh has lost 11 consecutive road games against Philadelphia, dating back to 1966. The Steelers' last victory in the City of Brotherly Love came on Oct. 24, 1965, when they defeated the Eagles 20-14 at Franklin Field. More than six decades later, the drought has stretched across three stadiums, multiple generations of players and several eras of Steelers football.

No state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide. When the judges of the International Court of Justice read out their verdict in the seven-year-old genocide case filed by The Gambia against Myanmar on Thursday, they could make history. In the years since the Genocide Convention was signed in 1948, after the Nazi Holocaust, dozens of individuals have been successfully prosecuted for the crime of genocide, in conflicts such as those in Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia. But no state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide.

The proposed Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill will also include capping ground rent at £250. The government is to introduce new laws to scrap the way flats are built in England and Wales. Under the proposed bill, most new leasehold flats will be banned and replaced with commonhold, where residents collectively own and manage their buildings. Matthew Pennycook, the housing minister, said the current leasehold system was "blighting lives" and was an "anachronism in the twenty-first century". The legislation follows Labour's 2024 election manifesto to "bring the feudal leasehold system to an end" - with further details expected to be set out later.

When the Vikings and 49ers face off in Mexico City on Sunday night, they'll be playing at the highest elevation any NFL game is ever played at: Estadio Azteca's altitude is around 7,300 feet. Kickers and physicists alike have agreed that high altitudes can easily add five yards or more to field goal range. The air is thinner at altitude, and in Mexico City the altitude makes the air about 20 percent less dense than at sea level. In Denver, which is about 2,000 feet lower than Mexico City, the air is about 15 percent less dense than at sea level, and Denver's Mile High Stadium is well known for the boost it gives to kickers.

Danish foreign minister says deal ‘removes all uncertainty’ over territory but warns trust in US needs rebuilding The Danish parliament has unanimously approved a new Arctic security pact between Greenland , Denmark and the US in what it is hoped will mark a new chapter in relations, months after Donald Trump’s threats to invade the largely autonomous territory. The deal, which was signed by the US president and the prime ministers of Greenland and Denmark, Jens-Frederik Nielsen and Mette Frederiksen, in September after months of talks, updates a 1951 defence agreement to give the US underwater access to Greenland and specific permission to construct a missile defence system.

It can develop into addiction, psychosis and violence, and has been linked to higher risk of ALS .

Obviously no one knew what WAR was back then, but his 1903 season was the equivalent of 5.5 bWAR, with 20 wins and a 2.30 ERA. He issued a lot of walks — 104 — but his 128 strikeouts, in an era when most batters didn't K much, ranked fifth in the National League. The following year, he struck out 177 in 307 innings, the K figure good for third in the league.

MLB seeks to redistribute player compensation within the league. While the union and league battle over the future of baseball's economics and are barreling toward a management lockout, a lesser-known element also lies at the heart of MLB's vision of the future. Team owners want to change the current separation between player compensation and their on-field value. According to MLB research presented this week to reporters, players with six years or fewer of major league service and not eligible for free agency delivered 71% of the league's total on-field value, as measured by wins over replacement (WAR). That group, however, received just 31% of the total compensation.

An Orange County legal court puts Fens on the basketball court, for now. Today's hearing in front of Judge Alyson Grine sought a Temporary Restraining Order (TRO), a legal mechanism now familiar to most college sports fans. A TRO grants one party in a lawsuit temporary relief while a legal argument proceeds in court. The basic idea is that a party suffering harm while the lawsuit unfolds cannot recover that harm even if he or she wins their case. In other words, Fens' lawyers today argued that Fens' suit has enough merit to be successful but that missing games now irreparably harms him. Those games can't be given back if he wins his suit in a few months.

Cumin-laced sodas are capturing a bigger market share in India as demand for homegrown flavours goes up. Saurabh Munjal, Nikhil Doda and Saurabh Bhutna - three cousins in India's north-western Punjab state - were messing about at home post dinner one evening, when Doda casually brewed up a tangy cumin-flavoured fizzy soda using regular pantry ingredients. Cumin-laced sodas had always been sold at street-side stalls in India, but it was a broken market of local companies. Not many had built a carbonated beverage brand around the flavour.

The final Turkey Day game is slated for 11 a.m. at Audubon High. The Green Wave enter the game with a 6-3 record under head coach Dan Reed while Haddon Township is 3-5 under head coach Bill Furlong. Audubon won a 56-0 decision in last year's meeting , one that featured Haddon Township's debut of its new artificial turf field as well as the game being broadcasted on SportsRadio 94.1 WIP's Turkey Bowl.

BYU’s corners will need to play well Saturday, as Kansas quarterback Isaiah Marshall is a dangerous dual-threat QB. BYU has never defeated Kansas and will make its final regular-season road trip of the season to Lawrence to take on the Jayhawks. On the line is a chance at the conference title game and a perch in the CFP rankings. The Cougars need star running back LJ Martin to fully return as a weapon. He's slowly returned to carry bigger loads the past two games. His backup Sione Moa, banged up in a win over Baylor needs to heal and get back on the field — but it won't be this week — as Preston Rex showed he has returned and is ready to contribute.

San Antonians will have to get creative if they want high school football on their TV screens. The UIL football state championships run from December 16 through December 19, as 12 champions will be crowned at AT&T Stadium. Fans unable to attend in person have had to rely on a carousel of TV stations broadcasting the games, and this year Nexstar and its network of stations are set to play all 12 games for free, according to the UIL's broadcast information. However, don't expect to catch the games on KENS 5. Nexstar may have acquired KENS 5 through its $6.2 billion acquisition of TEGNA and its numerous stations, but following the acquisition, Nexstar received a "Hold Separate Order" in April…

Bengals RB Chase Brown received national recognition for his two-touchdown performance and pass protection in Cincinnati's win over Pittsburgh. SB Nation's Doug Farrar named Brown among his AFC Secret Superstars for Week 10 on Wednesday, Nov. 18. Brown joined Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington and Indianapolis Colts cornerback Justin Walley on the list. The Bengals running back finished Sunday's 38-18 victory with 10 carries for 44 yards and eight receptions for 39 yards. He also caught two touchdown passes from Joe Burrow.

Ashleigh Barty is your 2026 International Tennis Hall of Fame inductee. Barty, whose retirement from the sport in 2022 stunned the tennis community, has joined... Barty , whose retirement from the sport in 2022 stunned the tennis community, has joined the likes of Roger Federer, Maria Sharapova and Martina Hingis in the Hall of Fame. The three-time major champion fought off competition from 2009 US Open champion Juan Martin del Potro and two-time Grand Slam champion Svetlana Kuznetsova – both of whom have missed out on joining the Hall of Fame for a second consecutive year.

Judge Alyson Grine granted a temporary restraining order that makes Fens immediately eligible after months of uncertainty . Fens filed a lawsuit Wednesday, Nov. 20, seeking a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction that would allow him to compete while his case proceeds in court. A hearing on the preliminary injunction is scheduled for 2 p.m. on Nov. 30, but Fens will remain eligible at least until that process is complete. The order will remain in effect until the judge rules on the motion for the injunction or until 5 p.m. on Dec. 1, whichever comes first.

Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI has finally been released after a 13-year wait since GTA V, when the ATP and WTA top 10s were filled... It has arguably been the most highly anticipated wait for a video game ever, with users now able to enjoy all that the exciting experience has to offer. The release coincides with a significant update in the tennis world, with the WTA year-end rankings having just been confirmed following the conclusion of the WTA Finals. The ATP will soon follow suit after the ATP Finals, which are currently underway in Turin.

RJ Luis Jr.'s time as a member of the LSU basketball team has been halted again after a statement from the LSU president Thursday night. On Thursday, Nov. 19, LSU President Wade Rousse instructed Will Wade to no longer play Luis following his Purple and Gold debut the day before against the University of Louisiana-Monroe.
